objective.statement: Group demisemiquavers (and the notes around them) so that every beat can be seen.
successCriteria: I beam the short notes of one beat together.
I start a new beam on each beat.
I do not beam across a beat line.

explanation.text: Short notes are easiest to read when they are beamed in beats. The rule is the one you know from quavers and semiquavers: join the notes of one beat with a beam, and never join notes from two different beats.

music.textAlternative: One bar of 2/4. Beat 1: four demisemiquavers and a quaver under one beam. Beat 2: a quaver and four demisemiquavers under one beam.

explanation.caption: 2/4: one beam for each crotchet beat.

explanation.text: In compound time the same rule applies to the dotted-crotchet beat: all the short notes of one beat share a beam, and a new beam starts on the next beat.

music.textAlternative: One bar of 6/8. Beat 1: four demisemiquavers and two quavers under one beam. Beat 2: a dotted crotchet.

explanation.caption: 6/8: the beam covers exactly the first beat.

explanation.text: A beam is a way of showing beats, so a beam that runs across a beat line is wrong, even if the notes add up. In this course a beat never has more than four demisemiquavers in a row, so every beat can be beamed with one beam. Demisemiquaver rests are arranged in the same way as semiquaver and quaver rests. Here you recognise them and compare their lengths; mixing them with notes inside one beat is left for later because its conventions are still to be confirmed.
One beam for each beat. Never beam across a beat line.

steps: Find the first beat: the first crotchet's worth of notes.
Check that one beam joins all the notes of that beat.
Check that a new beam starts on the second beat.

provenance.authoredBy: Music Theory Path curriculum team (Brief 05, drafted with AI assistance; pending qualified teacher review)
provenance.notes: Original wording. Follows Grade 3 outcome 3 and book section 4. The book also allows eight demisemiquavers in a crotchet beat to be beamed in two groups of four; the rule checker asks for one beam over the whole beat, so the course never uses more than four in a row (OPEN_QUESTIONS Q26, TEACHER TO CONFIRM). Dotted rests after short notes are not asked (Q4).
